2 In this appeal, filed under Section 23 of the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 (for short, 'the Act of 1987'), the challenge is to the judgment and order dated 21.09.2010, passed by the Railway Claims Tribunal, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur (for short 'the Tribunal'), whereby the claim filed by the respondents/claimants for compensation under Section 16 of the Act of 1987 was allowed.

sentences.text: Background facts:
Respondent No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
Respondent No. 3 is the son of the deceased.
The original respondent No. 2 died during the pendency of this appeal.
The respondents claim that on 26.02.2006, the deceased and respondent No.1 were proceeding to Nanded from Parbhani.
901.FA.347.2011 railway compensation judge.odt
It is stated that after purchasing the journey ticket, the deceased went ahead to occupy the seats.
He boarded the train.
The deceased accidentally fell from a moving train.
He sustained injuries and died.
According to the respondents, the death was in an untoward incident.
The deceased was a bona fide passenger.
4 The respondent-railway filed the written statement and opposed the claim.
It was contended that the death was not in an untoward incident.
The deceased was negligent.
He sustained injuries due to his criminal act.
The death, according to the railway, was therefore not in an untoward incident.
5 Before the Tribunal, the respondent No.1 examined herself as a witness.
The evidence was not adduced by the railway.
Learned Member of the Tribunal, on the basis of the evidence, allowed the claim.
The appellant-railway, being aggrieved by the judgment and order, is in appeal before 901.FA.347.2011 railway compensation judge.odt
this Court

.

I have heard the learned Advocate Ms Neerja Chaubey for the appellant and the learned Advocate Mr A. B. Deshpande for the respondents.
Perused the record and proceedings.

7 In the facts and circumstances, the following points fall for my determination:
(i) Whether the deceased died in an untoward incident as understood by the provisions of Section 123(c)(2) of the Railways Act, 1989?
(ii) Whether the deceased was a bona fide passenger travelling with a valid journey ticket?

8 Learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that considering the injuries sustained by the deceased, the possibility of the deceased falling from the moving train has 901.FA.347.2011 railway compensation judge.odt been completely ruled out.
Learned Advocate submitted that evidence and circumstances clearly show that the deceased was run over by an unknown train at the spot of the incident.
Learned Advocate further submitted that in the application, respondent No.1 nowhere stated that she was travelling with the deceased.
Learned Advocate submitted that the learned Member has failed to consider the evidence in proper perspective.

9 Learned Advocate for the respondents submitted that simply because the body of the deceased was cut into two pieces from the waist, it would not be sufficient to conclude that it was a case of run over.
Learned Advocate submitted that such injuries are possible even in a fall from a slow-moving train.
Learned Advocate submitted that the learned Member of the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record.
Learned Advocate submitted that the ticket recovered was a valid journey ticket for two adult passengers.
Learned 901.FA.347.2011
railway compensation judge.odt Advocate submitted that this fact fortifies the contention of respondent No.1 that she and the deceased were travelling together from Parbhani to Nanded.
10 In order to appreciate the rival submissions, I have minutely perused the record and proceedings.
The deceased was a bona fide passenger travelling with a valid journey ticket.
The journey ticket was recovered at the time of the inquest panchanama.
The ticket was duly verified and it was found to be a valid journey ticket.
In her evidence, AW-1-Vaishali Makalwar has stated that after purchasing the ticket at Parbhani railway station, her husband proceeded towards the platform to occupy the seat in the compartment.
She has stated that there was a heavy rush of passengers on the platform.
She has stated that her husband went ahead and boarded the train, but she could not board the said train due to a heavy rush.
Later on, she travelled to Nanded by another train.
She has stated that at Nanded she came to know that her husband was 901.FA.347.2011 railway compensation judge.odt found at Parbhani railway station in an injured condition.
The ticket recovered was a valid journey ticket for two adult passengers.

3 No.1 in her evidence has stated the purpose of their visit to Nanded.
This evidence, in my opinion, is sufficient to accept the contention of respondent No.1 that she was travelling with the deceased from Parbhani to Nanded.
11 The railway has pleaded the defence of negligence.
It is contended that the injuries sustained by the deceased indicate that the deceased was run over by some unknown train while crossing the railway line.
The DRM inquiry report is part of the record.
In the DRM report, it is nowhere stated that the deceased was either run over or dashed by the train at the spot of the incident.

On the contrary, the conclusion arrived at by the DRM indicates that the deceased, while boarding the train,
either from the off side or from the platform side, in a negligent manner, fell down and died.
railway compensation judge.odt my view, this report of the DRM inquiry is sufficient to reject the defence put forth in the written statement about negligence.
12 It is further pertinent to note that the railway has not examined any witnesses.
There is no document on record to show that the deceased at the spot of the incident was run over by the train.
There is no report of the loco-pilot of any train or the guard of any train.
This fact is against the case of the appellant.
As far as the defence of negligence is concerned, in my view, in the facts and circumstances, it may not be available to the appellant-railway.
As far as this issue is concerned, the legal position has been enunciated by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
It would be useful to make a reference to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Union of India .v/s. Rina Devi 1.
Para No. 25 is relevant for this purpose.

It is extracted below:
1 (2019) 3 SCC 572 901.FA.347.2011 railway compensation judge.odt "25.
We are unable to uphold the above view as the concept of 'self inflicted injury' would require intention to inflict such injury and not mere negligence of any particular degree.
Doing so would amount to invoking the principle of contributory negligence which cannot be done in the case of liability based on 'no fault theory'.

We may in this connection refer to judgment of this Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. versus Sunil Kumar laying down that plea of negligence of the victim cannot be allowed in claim based on 'no fault theory'
under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sentences.text: Accordingly, we hold that death or injury in the course of boarding or de-boarding a train will be an 'untoward incident' entitling a victim to the compensation and will not fall under the proviso to Section 124-A merely on the plea of negligence of the victim as a contributing factor."
13 In Rina Devi (supra) , the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the principle of contributory negligence cannot be invoked in case of liability based on 'no fault theory'.
It is held that the liability to pay compensation under the Act of 1989 is based on 'no fault theory'.

It is held that death or injury in the course of boarding or de-boarding train will be an untoward incident entitling the victim to compensation and will not fall under the Proviso to Section 124A, merely on the plea of The Union Of India, General Manager vs Smt. 4 901.FA.347.2011 railway compensation judge.odt negligence of the victim as a contributing factor.
In my view, the law laid down in Rina Devi (supra), supports the contention of the respondents/claimants.
14 In this case, the evidence is sufficient to prove that the deceased boarded the train at Parbhani Railway Station to go to Nanded.
There is no eyewitness to the incident.
Injuries sustained by the deceased could be possible due to a fall from a slow-moving train.
The incident occurred at Parbhani railway station.
It is common knowledge that at the platform, the train moves slowly.
In case of fall of a passenger from a slow moving train, the possibility of the passenger getting stuck in any part of the railway and in the process, coming under the wheel can't be ruled out.
In this case, simply because of the nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased it could not be positively concluded that the deceased was run over by the train.
Such injuries could be possible due to a fall from a slow-moving train.
Learned Member of the Tribunal has considered the 901.FA.347.2011 railway compensation judge.odt facts and evidence in great detail.
I do not see any reason to find fault with the judgment and order passed by the learned Member of the Tribunal.
The findings are based on a proper appreciation of the evidence.
As such, I conclude that there is no substance in the appeal.
Therefore, I answer both points in the affirmative.
15 In this case, the accident had occurred on 26.02.2006.

Learned Advocate for the respondents submitted that after issuance of notification dated 22.12.2016 by the Ministry of Railways (Railway Board), the compensation payable under the various entries of Schedule to the Railway Accidents and Untoward Incidents (Compensation) Rules, 1990 has been revised with effect from 01.01.2017.

sentences.text: In view of the amendment of the schedule, in case of a death claim, the claimants are entitled to get compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-.

However, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in 901.FA.347.2011 railway compensation judge.odt the Case of Union of India .v/s. Radha Yadav 2 in the case of the old claim, the respondents/claimants would be entitled to get compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- without interest, if the compensation awarded earlier with interest is less than Rs.8,00,000/-.
Learned Advocate for the claimants submitted that the compensation awarded earlier i.e. Rs.4,00,000/- with interest, would not be more than Rs.8,00,000/-.
Therefore, in this case, the claimants would be entitled to get Rs.8,00,000/- without interest.
16 Accordingly, I pass the following order:
(i) The first appeal stands dismissed.

(ii) The judgment and order dated 21.09.2010 passed by the Railway Claims Tribunal, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur in Claim Application No.
81/OA-II/RCT/ NGP/2006 stands modified.
